text: Hi Maria! Today we'll work on a coding problem. Given an array of integers and a target sum, find two distinct numbers that add up to the target. How would you approach this?
Okay, let me think... So the problem is about find two numbers that sum to target, right? I think in use a brute force first. Like, I check every pair of numbers.
Sure, walk me through the brute force approach and its complexity.

So with brute force I use two loops. The first loop go through each number, and the second loop check all the other numbers to see if they sum to target. This is O of n squared because I have two nested loops. Is not very efficient.
Good analysis. Can you think of a more optimal solution?

Yes, actually I can use a hash map. So I iterate through the array one time. For each number I calculate the complement, which is target minus current number. Then I check if complement exist in the hash map. If yes, I found the pair. If no, I add current number to the hash map. This way is O of n for time and O of n for space.

Hmm, edge cases... I think if the array is empty or have only one element, then is impossible to find pair so I return empty. Also if there is duplicate numbers I need to be careful. For example if target is 6 and array have two 3s, the hash map need to handle this correctly. I think my solution work because I check the complement before add the number.
